items.title: Email Campaign · : 1-Year Annual Service (warm, revenue-now)
items.preview:
**1. Campaign name + audience**
- Name: `Year 1 Annual Service Reminder`
- Audience: 16 clients hitting 12 months post-install this week (triggered send, not a list blast)
**2. Subject line + alternates** (all under 60 char, no dashes)
- Primary (specific): `It's been about a year. Time for your annual service.`
- Alt 1 (curiosity): `A quick check-in on your water system`
- Alt 2 (authority): `Your first annual service is due`
- Alt 3 (pain): `One year in. Let's keep your water exactly right.`
- Alt 4 (specific): `Your 12-month service window is open`
**3. Preview text** (under 90 char)
`Low-maintenance by design. But year one is when we come take a look.`
**4. Body draft** (legacy system names suppressed per Rule 2, tenure line used)
> Hi Joseph,
>
> It's been about a year since we installed your ClearWave system, and that means you're due for your first annual service.
>
> Our systems are engineered to run quietly in the background, so you probably haven't thought about it much. That's the point. But year one is when we come out, check everything over, and make sure it keeps performing exactly the way it should.
>
> Just reply to this email or give us a call and we'll get you on the schedule. It's an easy visit.
>
> Thanks for being a ClearWave customer.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
*(Note: sign-off printed exactly two lines, no em dash prefix per Rule 4. For Steven Bradham the same tenure line applies since "Ferromax + Ironmax + RO" is legacy. No current-brand names appear in this group, so all 16 use the tenure line.)*
**5. Send timing**
Tuesday, 10:00 AM ET. Midweek mid-morning for a service/transactional-feel email; highest reply likelihood for a "reply to schedule" CTA.
**6. Expected performance**
- Open: 55 to 65% (well above your 42.3% baseline; this is a triggered, personally relevant, transactional-tone email to 16 warm clients, not a promo blast)
- Click/reply: 15 to 25% (reply-to-schedule lowers friction vs. a link click)
- Conversion (booked service): 6 to 9 of 16. Real revenue this week from a nearly free send.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from the **Jobber lifecycle trigger: 1-year annual service candidates (16)**. Aligns with Rule 1 (12-month floor met, annual service is the correct first touch), Rule 2 (tenure line for legacy names), and MAILCHIMP HEALTH (small triggered send to rehab sender reputation vs. fatigued full-list blasts).
---

items.title: Email Campaign · : Referral Push (30 to 60 days post-install)
items.preview:
**1. Campaign name + audience**
- Name: `New Client Referral Invite`
- Audience: 30 clients 30 to 60 days post-install, satisfied (triggered send)
**2. Subject line + alternates** (under 60 char, no dashes)
- Primary (specific): `Know someone with bad water? There's $500 in it.`
- Alt 1 (curiosity): `A quick favor (and a real thank you)`
- Alt 2 (pain): `Who do you know fighting their water?`
- Alt 3 (authority): `Our best clients come from our best clients`
- Alt 4 (specific): `$500 per referral. Here's how it works.`
**3. Preview text** (under 90 char)
`If you've enjoyed your water so far, someone you know deserves the same.`
**4. Body draft**
For clients with a legacy system (most of this group), e.g. Lee Offen / Feroz Tamana:
> Hi Lee,
>
> You've had your ClearWave system for about a month now, and by now the water probably just feels like the new normal. That's exactly how it should feel.
>
> Here's the ask. Most of our best clients come to us because someone they trust made an introduction. If you know a friend, neighbor, or family member fighting their water, we'll take great care of them.
>
> How it works:
> - They book a free water assessment through you.
> - If they become a client, you get $500 cash. (It climbs to $750 after five referrals in a year, and $1,000 after ten.)
> - Even if they just book a consult and don't move forward, you get a $50 gift card.
>
> Just reply with a name, or send them our way and tell them to mention you.
>
> Thanks for trusting us with your home.
>
> Justin
> CEO / ClearWave
For Janine Stenson (system field is a **current** brand name, so it may be named):
> Hi Janine,
>
> You've had your ClearWave Sovereign for about a month now...
*(Same body otherwise. Only Janine in this sample carries a current ClearWave name; the rest use the tenure line per Rule 2.)*
**5. Send timing**
Thursday, 11:00 AM ET. Late-week mid-morning performs well for a low-pressure "favor" ask; gives them the weekend to think of names.
**6. Expected performance**
- Open: 48 to 58% (recent installs, still in the honeymoon window, name recognition high)
- Click/reply: 8 to 14%
- Conversion (referral name submitted): 3 to 6 names across 30 sends. Each closed name is worth far more than the send costs, and this is the single highest-LTV lever available this week.
**7. Source justification**
Draws from **Jobber lifecycle trigger: referral push candidates (30)** and the **REFERRAL BONUS STRUCTURE** (exact $500 / $750 / $1,000 / $50 figures used). Complies with Rule 3 (referrals, no review ask), Rule 3a ("free water assessment" used verbatim), and Rule 2 (tenure line vs. named current brand handled correctly).
---
### Why not the other three this week
- **Cold 1,000 re-engagement:** high potential, but sending to 1,000 cold contacts while your open rate is at 0.2 to 0.4% risks further deliverability damage. Run it *after* two clean triggered sends lift your reputation. Worth a dedicated proposal next week with a fresh water-news value angle.
- **Concierge (100):** eligible on the 12-month rule, but it's a considered upsell best sent as its own "is Concierge worth it for me? here's the math" email, not competing for attention this week.
- **RO replacement (29):** viable, but overlaps in tone with annual service. Sequence it next.

---
